description: Sabotages for win-text-sys. Run with tools/run-sabotage.ps1; see tools/README-sabotage.md for the format and for why the results are read the way they are.
notCoveredHere: The counts are never passed as the page's -1. A sabotage that passed -1 for a count would make the call read each slice as a NUL-terminated string, which a slice is not, so it would read past the slice's end: the embedded-NUL test would catch it, but by whatever the memory past a Vec holds, which is not a result to record. A slice of more than i32::MAX units cannot be made by a test, so the refusal's limit is observed through the function that makes the counts and not through compare_string_ordinal.

sabotages.name: WT-1: the less-than result is reported as greater
sabotages.why: The two orderings are the same shape in the match, so a swap compiles; every comparison of unequal strings then reads backwards.

sabotages.name: WT-1: the equal result is reported as less
sabotages.why: Equality is what the workspace's name matching reads, so it has to be the one result that is reported as itself.

sabotages.name: WT-1: a result the page does not list is reported as equal
sabotages.why: A value the call should never give must not be read as a successful match.

sabotages.name: WT-1: a zero result does not report the call's last error
sabotages.why: The code is the one thing the failure carries; without it a caller cannot tell a call's refusal from no code at all.

sabotages.name: WT-1: a case-insensitive comparison is made case-sensitive
sabotages.why: The flag is the only thing that separates the two; folding case is observed by comparing strings that differ only in case.

sabotages.name: WT-1: a case-sensitive comparison is made case-insensitive
sabotages.why: The opposite direction: a comparison that was asked to take the units as they are folds them.

sabotages.name: WT-1: the two strings are passed in each other's place
sabotages.why: A comparison of unequal strings reads backwards, and swapping the arguments no longer reverses the result.

sabotages.name: WT-1: a length is truncated to the count instead of refused
sabotages.why: A length above i32::MAX would wrap to a small or negative count, and the call would compare a different string, or take a negative count as the page's -1.

sabotages.name: WT-1: the second string is named as the first when it is too long
sabotages.why: The refusal names the string; a caller that reports which one is too long reports the wrong one.

sabotages.name: WT-1: the second length is checked before the first
sabotages.why: When both strings are too long the first is the one named; the order of the two checks is that guarantee.
replace:
let second = count(Operand::Second, second)?;
    Ok((count(Operand::First, first)?, second))

sabotages.name: WT-1: the call's failure has no source
sabotages.why: The code is the failure's cause; dropping it as the source leaves an error chain that stops at the wrapper.

sabotages.name: WT-1 control: the equal result is reported through a binding
sabotages.why: A control: the same ordering through a local, which no test can tell apart. A sweep that reports it caught is reporting everything caught and proves nothing.
